headline: Approved sending bedrock removal rule changes to City Council on a 5-2 vote; rejected a City Center TDR option.
summary: Staff also discussed transfer of development rights, and members rejected applying them in City Center above five or six stories. A public hearing on LDR-26-12 technical amendments was set for 24 November. Members agreed to take housing and cultural and arts plan ideas to the City Council.
decisions: Approved LDR-26-01 bedrock removal language and report and forwarded them to City Council, 5-2 vote, with Mittag and Moscatelli opposed.
Approved warning LDR-26-12 for a public hearing on 24 November 2026 at 7 p.m. and approved its report, unanimously.
Reopened the continued public hearing and kept it open to 10 November, unanimously.
Rejected applying TDRs in City Center above the 5-6 stories allowed before the 2025 amendments.
Agreed to present the housing action plan and cultural and arts plan ideas to City Council for a Municipal Planning Grant.
Agreed to have no second meeting in December.

plain_text:
PAGE 1 
SOUTH BURLINGTON PLANNING COMMISSION 
27 OCTOBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington Planning Commission held a regular meeting on Tuesday, 
27 October 2026, at 7:00 p.m., in Room 301, City Hall, 180 Market Street, and via 
Zoom. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: J. Louisos, Chair; M. Mittag, D. MacDonald, J. Moscatelli, D. 
Leban, C. Lawrence, M. Emery 
 
ALSO PRESENT: P. Conner, Director of Planning and Zoning; K. Peterson, City 
Planner; R. Doyle, C. Gendron, T. Barritt, E. Fitzgerald    
 
1. Instructions on exiting the building in case of an emergency: 
 
Ms. Louisos provided instructions on emergency exit from the building. 
 
 
2. Agenda: Additions, deletions or changes in order of agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the agenda. 
 
3. Open to the public for items not related to the Agenda: 
 
No issues were raised. 
 
4. Planning Commissioner announcements and staff report: 
 
Staff is working with the Regional Planning Commission (CCRPC) regarding the 
Housing Action Plan. 
 
The draft of the final Parks & Recreation Master Plan will be presented to the City 
Council on 7 December.
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 2 
Last Friday, the City submitted “Step 3” for the City Center “Downtown” 
designation. 
 
Mr. Conner said he has been invited to be a panelist for UVM’s release of their 
“Climate Assessment in Vermont.” 
 
Ms. Louisos advised that she attended the Regional Planning conference last 
week. 
 
5. Public Hearing on LDR-26-11 on the Act 250 Tier 1A Review of Conditions 
Process: 
 
Ms. Peterson said the amendment needs to be include in the Tier 1A process.  It 
relates to conditions which can go to local review.  This has to be done by the 
DRB, and this amendment grants them this authority.  The rest of the application 
can be handled administratively. 
 
Ms. Emery moved to open the public hearing.  Mr. MacDonald seconded.  Motion 
passed unanimously. 
 
Ms. Louisos asked for public comment.  There was no public comment. 
 
Mr. Moscatelli moved to close the public hearing.  Mr. MacDonald seconded.  The 
motion passed unanimously. 
 
6. Staff Tier 1A Status Update:     
 
Mr. Conner reviewed other needed amendments including: 
 
a. An amendment regarding rare and endangered species 
b. A technical item needed for review 
c. A stand-alone amendment upgrading the bedrock standards 
adopted last year (the Commission had decided to wait for a full 
board before voting) 
 
Mr. Conner felt the cleanest way to handle these was to put them all into one 
“bucket” to go to the City Council on 8 November. 
 
The City received comments back regarding its Tier 1A application.  These were 
mostly questions.  The City will need to provide adopted language for the final
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 3 
application.  Staff has started to draft narratives as to how the City has looked at 
individual natural resources.  There will be a meeting with A & R later this week to 
discuss this further. 
 
Ms. Peterson said the Commission will need to reopen the public hearing and 
keep it open to 10 November.   
 
Ms. Louisos moved to reopen the continued public hearing.  Ms. Emery seconded.  
Motion passed unanimously. 
 
7. LDR 26-01 Bedrock Removal: Possible action to advance amendments and 
associated Report to the City Council: 
 
Mr. MacDonald moved to approve the language of LDR-26-01 and the associated 
report and forward it to the City Council.  Ms. Louisos seconded. 
 
Ms. Emery asked what determines what is “reasonable.”  She noted that in the 
past, this has been an issue.   
 
Mr. Mittag said he would like to amend the allowable hours in a residential district 
to Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.  He felt there should be no weekend hours 
when there are families gathered.  He said this has been a problem in the past, 
and he felt it would happen again.  He also agreed that “reasonable” has been 
notoriously difficult to deal with. 
 
Mr. Doyle said some schools are not in residential districts, and this could affect 
the operations of a school.   
 
Mr. Moscatelli stressed that there has not been unanimous support of the 
proposed amendment.  He also said that it is asking the DRB to make its own 
rules.  He said what the Commission should do is to rescind this amendment and 
strengthen the Noise Ordinance.  He was concerned that the amendment has no 
caps which could lead to the same problems that happened before.  He also felt 
the amendment does not do what was intended and makes situations harder to 
deal with in the future. 
 
Ms. Leban said that too many “if, ands, and buts” could stop development.  She 
said the Commission to put in language asking developers to “be aware before 
you start.”  She acknowledged that they are stuck in a hard position: not wanting
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 4 
undue noise and not wanting to stop development.  They tried to stress pre-
planning discussion to limit the amount of damage. 
 
In the vote that followed the motion passed 5-2 with Mr. Mittag and Mr. Moscatelli 
voting against. 
 
8. LDR-26-12 – Minor technical amendments and possible warning of Public 
Hearing and approval of associated Planning Commission Report: 
 
Ms. Peterson outlined the two technical amendments: 
 
1. Regarding Form Based Code: it was not clear which regulations 
applied to the Form Based Code District.  This amendment makes 
it clear. 
2. Conforms to State Statute which now says an additional dwelling 
unit (ADU) no longer has the requirement for the owner to occupy 
the premises.   
 
Ms. Leban asked whether all Form Based Code projects that were approved 
comply with the regulations.  Mr. Conner said they did. 
 
Mr. Mittaq moved to warn LDR-26-12 for public hearing on 24 November 2026 at 7 
p.m. and to approve the accompanying report.  Ms. Leban seconded.  The motion 
passed unanimously. 
 
9. Continued Review of Transfer of Development Rights (TDRs): 
 
Mr. Conner said staff would like direction on what, if anything, the Commission 
wants to do regarding TDRs.   
 
1. He suggested they could potentially allow a reduction in minimum 
lot size from 5000 sq. ft.  He directed attention to graphics 
showing what this could look like.  He also noted that TDRs are 
expensive to transact.   
 
2. This option was already rejected. 
 
3. Mr. Mittag said 2000 sq. ft. seems reasonable.  Ms. Leban asked if 
this apples to apartments in addition to houses.  Mr. Conner said it 
applies to the unit, not to the building.  Mr. Mittag asked how
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 5 
much above 2000 sq. ft. would you have to go to need a TDR.  Ms. 
Leban said anything above 2500 should require a TDR.   
 
Mr. Laurence asked how many TDRs are out there.  Mr. Conner said there are 800 
that have not been used, 400 of which are unsevered. 
 
Mr. Conner showed a graph of distribution of square footage build after 1990 and 
after 2010 in single family or condos.  He noted that for the past 20 years, no 
ownership multi-family buildings are being built. 
 
Mr. Conner said the challenge of the current system is that it is beyond the current 
market.  Ms. Peterson added that TDRs are being used one at a time because they 
are so very expensive.  She cited costs for title searches, surveys, etc., as they 
have to identify the exact piece of property being severed. 
 
Mr. Mittag said the market for TDRs has been restricted because developers aren’t 
doing large developments now. 
 
Mr. MacDonald said he does not favor any of this as he felt it was unnecessary. 
 
Mr. Doyle suggested going away from square footage to “built over space.”  He 
said land is where taxable revenue comes from.  He suggested looking at 
“footprint area.” 
 
Mr. Gendron questioned whether a developer should have to pay for extra height 
when it is required for operational efficiency.  He noted issues involving Beta and 
the challenges they are facing.  They can need up to 40 feet in height for a one-
story building to house aircraft.  To go to a needed 50 or 51 feet could cost them 
$500,000.  They currently have to pay for each additional 14 feet. 
 
Ms. Leban said when the Commission adopted this, they were not thinking about 
commercial or industrial buildings.  Mr. Gendron said their industrial buildings 
could need giant simulators. 
 
Ms. Emery said houses should be designed to support the City Plan goals.  
Houses with thousands of square feet do not do that.  She felt there should be 
some kind of exchange so the City Plan is upheld.
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 6 
Mr. Conner questioned what threshold could trigger a TDR, and what the TDR 
would be worth.  Ms. Louisos said that for discussion she would suggest 2000 sq. 
ft. and $2000.  Mr. Conner said staff could run the numbers to see what that would 
trigger. 
  
Mr. Laurence asked whether it would work to use the building footprint.  Mr. 
Conner said it is possible.  One question is whether 1 to 4-units buildings would 
be the same and whether this would discourage 4-unit buildings.  There is also 
the question of staircases, etc.   
 
Mr. Conner also cited the challenge of individuals who choose a larger lot with a 
sprawling house.  They will do what they want to do, and it won’t influence TDRs. 
 
Mr. Mittag asked Mr. Gendron what would be a reasonable area and price.  Mr. 
Gendron suggested he get together with staff and discuss this. 
 
4. There was little interest in this option. 
 
5. The Commission did not pursue this option. 
 
6. Adjust what a TDR is worth in the receiving area: Mr. Conner said 
this speaks to a future market as it is hard to talk about “now.”  
There have been no inquiries regarding a 7-story building on 
Shelburne Road.  Ms. Emery said she didn’t want to dissuade a 
new industry because they can’t afford TDRs.  Mr. Mittag stressed 
that the objective is to expand the TDR market.  Ms. Louisos said 
she is not inclined to change the value of a TDR.  Ms. Leban noted 
that a 2500 sq. ft. house now costs $1,000,000, so another $10,000 
doesn’t mean anything.  She also said if only 800 additional 
square footage is needed, why should the builder pay for 2000.  
Also, if they are paying for it, they would probably find ways to 
use it, adding to the building. 
 
Mr. Mittag said the City instituted TDRs in order to conserve land.  People bought 
into that, and now they have conserved land for which they haven’t sold their 
TDRs.   
 
7. Apply TDRs in City Center at some threshold above the 5-6 stories 
allowed prior to the 2025 amendments: Mr. Laurence said he
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 7 
wasn’t sure adding barriers to City Center development meets the 
City’s objectives.  Mr. Conner noted there is a point at which a 
building has to go to steel.  He did not think it likely they will see a 
9 or 10 story building.  Mr. Mittag said that in Scandinavia they 
are building skyscrapers of all wood. 
 
Mr. Mittag suggested they might want taller buildings north of Williston Road.  He 
cited the need for affordable housing.  He suggested possibly 8 stories in T3 and 
10 in T5.  Ms. Leblan cited the breakdown when you have parking under the 
building.  It is so expensive, you have to go up.  She said there is already so much 
complication.  She did not want to add more.  She noted that in Burlington, they 
wound up shortening buildings. 
 
Members decided to reject #7. 
 
8. Municipal Planning Grant: 
 
Mr. Conner presented two ideas, both of which are in the City Plan: 
 
a. Housing action plan 
b. Cultural and arts plan 
 
He suggested presenting both to the City Council.  Members agreed. 
 
9. Landscaping amended project charge to add Commercial District 
Civic Spaces: 
 
Ms. Peterson reviewed the history.  She noted instances where the cost of a 
building is incredibly high, and the cost of required landscaping can maximize out 
ground space.  There is also a question of how much civic space should there be 
in residential vs. commercial/industrial districts.  She asked members if the 
favored adding this to their project charge.   
 
Mr. Moscatelli moved to amend the project charge to the language provided in 
the meeting packet.  Mr. MacDonald seconded.   
 
Mr. Gendron said they are putting in landscaping because they have to, not 
because it is meaningful.  He cited a lot of challenges.
PLANNING COMMISSION 27 October 2026 PAGE 8 
Ms. Louisos noted a beautiful stormwater facility and hoped to hear from those 
people. 
 
Ms. Moscatelli asked if the City Arborist is involved in this discussion.  Ms. 
Peterson said he is along with a tree specialist. 
 
 10. Other Business: 
 
a. Receipt of Condemnation Hearing Notice 
b. Members agreed to have no second meeting in December. 
c. Ms. Emery said she is reaching out to people to talk about the 
future of cities. 
 
The question arose as to whether landscaping regulations have been combined 
with DPW specs.  Mr. Conner said the LDR regulations predate DPWs.  Anything 
that is technical staff will update.  
 
As there was no further business to come before the Commission, the meeting 
was adjourned by common consent at 9:02 p.m. 
 
 
 
    ___________________________________ 
     Clerk
